target_customer: Startup founders hiring their first international contractors and employees
problem: Hiring abroad requires localized contracts, compliance and local currency payouts that are slow and expensive. Shor offers contractor payments in 150+ countries and employer of record in about 70 markets with a disclosed FX margin.
business_model: Per person monthly fees ($19 contractor, $299 EOR, about $50 to $60 own entity) plus a 2% FX margin, per the company site
product_category: International payroll and employer of record

founders.name: Daivik Goel
education: University of Waterloo, BASc Computer Engineering
previous_startups: Founders Brew, a founder community of 2,000+ across San Francisco, Toronto and New York
founders.background_notes: From the YC page, which lists product and engineering work at Tesla, Cisco Meraki and early-stage startups.

founders.name: Avi Konduru
previous_startups: Rent-to-own home exchange that facilitated over $2M in sales (outcome not stated)

competitors.name: Rise
competitors.what: Crypto-native EOR and payroll platform with in-house stablecoin infrastructure
competitors.traction_then: Press release in March 2025 describes accelerating stablecoin payroll adoption; $1B payroll volume claimed by November 2025 on its own blog

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi-country payroll relies on local partners and entities; the engineering is workflow and payments integration, with stablecoin settlement adding moderate complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Deel, Remote and Rippling dominate global payroll and many added stablecoin payouts, so price and speed are copyable; founder community distribution is the only edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Deel announced stablecoin salary payouts on February 10, 2026, per an industry guide, showing incumbents absorbing the stablecoin wedge.

market_need_then: Founders hiring abroad face setup time, legal cost and FX fees; the YC launch positions Shor as the fastest and cheapest option. Competitors such as Rise show demand for stablecoin payroll in 2025.

branding.domain_note: Uses shorpay.com; the YC launch page and a podcast page reference tryshor.com, so two domains are in use.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, founder to founder; 'Built by founders, for founders' with a Slack channel with a founder instead of a support queue.

branding.community_and_virality: The CEO also runs Founders Brew, a community of 2,000+ founders, a possible distribution channel; no source ties it to Shor sales.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear founder-first voice and community link, but no press about the brand and the name resembles Shor's algorithm and other uses.

pivots.from: Earlier idea before the YC pivot (not described in sources found)
pivots.to: Contractor payroll, shipped within about a week, then international payroll and EOR
pivots.why: A founder interview summary says the contractor product was built during a YC pivot; the reason is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Shor is an active Summer 2025 company that launched international payroll and EOR in 2025 with stated backing from Polychain Capital, Founders Capital and Goodwater, though amounts are not public. The CEO's Founders Brew community gives a distribution channel. No acquisition or shutdown news exists. Deel and others added stablecoin payouts by 2026, so the wedge faces strong incumbents.
notes: Investor names come from the company's own YC page and site and a YESPress profile; the round has no amount, date or stage in any source, so stage is recorded as other. VCBacked lists $500K pre-seed with only Y Combinator as investor, which conflicts and is not recorded. The pivot detail comes from a secondary profile of a founder interview and is not verified. The dating of the round to 2025 is based on the company being founded in 2025. Pricing differs across sources ($20 versus $19 contractor); the company site was used.
